paper.title: ARISE: Agent Reasoning with Intrinsic Skill Evolution in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
paper.central_claim: ARISE: a hierarchical RL framework where a shared policy is both Skills Manager and Worker; it selects skills by log-prob scoring, distills successful traces into a two-tier skill library, and a hierarchical reward co-evolves reasoning and library; outperforms GRPO-family and memory-augmented baselines, especially out of distribution, and each component contributes.

evidence.quote: Within a rollout group containing both
evidence.support_explanation: The authors' argument for the hierarchical reward assumes R=2 and R=1 trajectories coexist in a group.

evidence.quote: assigns trajectories with
evidence.support_explanation: Opus inference from the paper's own Eqs. 5 and 7 and O01/O02. The gate is a query-level test (max_k p_k ≥ δ), so each group is all-skill or all-no-skill, and rewards are {0,2} or {0,1}. Eq. 5's (r−μ_G)/(σ_G+ϵ) is invariant to rescaling the rewards, so a {0,2} group gets the same advantages as a {0,1} group. 'Both outcomes coexist in the same group' never occurs. The hierarchical reward cannot change the policy gradient as described, and the EMA utilities it feeds are only rescaled (rank-preserving). The binary-reward ablation's reported effect is therefore unexplained by the written algorithm.

evidence.quote: it is inserted into the cache with initial utility
evidence.support_explanation: New skills enter at u=0.

evidence.quote: the entry with the lowest utility is moved to the reservoir
evidence.support_explanation: With a full cache of selected skills whose EMA utility is >0 (R≥0, positive whenever solved), a new u=0 skill is the eviction target. Reservoir skills are never selected, so their utility never updates (C.2 Update) and Load cannot promote them. Late-stage specialised skills (Table 8) are hard to reconcile with this rule.

signatures.object: Tiered skill library: cache (Cc=10) + reservoir (Cr=100) of 220-char JSON skill documents (name, problem_type, key_insight, 2-3 method steps, check), each with EMA utility
signatures.information: Query + positive-advantage solution traces (<=2, clipped 400 chars) from the same GRPO group, ground-truth correctness reward; no access to test problems
signatures.operation: Dedicated rollout O_{G+1} by the same policy summarizes successes into one skill; four-stage format validation; Add -> Evict/Load/Delete by utility
signatures.output: Updated cache/reservoir; fallback 'trace_abstract' skill if JSON invalid (<15% of attempts after warm-up)
signatures.feedback: r_task correctness and r_skill bonus -> hierarchical reward R in {0,1,2}; utility u<-0.9u+0.1R for selected skill
signatures.selection_rule_data: Admission = format validity only (no marginal-gain/regression test); retention = lowest-utility eviction, reservoir deletion if bottom-10% utility and zero usage; utility is raw reward EMA (confounded by difficulty per App.D.3)
signatures.persistence: Library persists across training steps (state of ES-MDP); no versioning, rollback or dedup/merge of content
signatures.later_use: Cache entries scored for every later query in Phase II
signatures.claimed_effect: Library grows to ~50-80 skills before Phase II and specializes (App.E.2); ablation without O_{G+1} lowers AIME24 56.4->55.0
signatures.failure_boundary: Duplicate/conflicting skills never merged; evaluation-time library state unspecified; math-only

signatures.object: Skill selection/injection read path (not a separate learned retriever)
signatures.information: Query and cache skill texts (truncated to 128 tokens); policy conditional log-prob s_k
signatures.operation: softmax(s_k/sigma) with epsilon-greedy (0.1) and confidence gate delta=0.35; selected skill prepended with 'SKILL:' prefix
signatures.output: Skill-conditioned rollouts (73% utilization) or unaided rollouts
signatures.feedback: Hierarchical reward gives correct-with-skill advantage over correct-unaided
signatures.selection_rule_data: Selection draw z_t has no loss term in Eq.6; bonus shapes worker's use of injected skills, not an explicitly credited selection action
signatures.persistence: Not persistent per se; depends on S1 library and on policy weights
signatures.later_use: Every Phase II rollout and evaluation
signatures.claimed_effect: Policy gradient directly shapes selection; random selection ablation 55.1 vs 56.4 AIME24
signatures.failure_boundary: Low delta over-injects (89% use, -1.2 AIME24); high delta suppresses use

signatures.object: Model weights trained with GRPO jointly with S1/S2 (boundary component, not itself the retained harness object)
signatures.information: Group-relative advantages over G=8 rollouts with DAPO dynamic sampling
signatures.operation: 500-step warm-up with binary reward, then 1,500 steps with skill-augmented hierarchical reward
signatures.output: Policy that conditions on SKILL: prefix
signatures.claimed_effect: +1.8~3.5 points over GRPO on 7 benchmarks across 2 backbones
signatures.failure_boundary: Gain for binary-reward variant is ~0.6 AIME24 over GRPO (E021)

gap.author_gap: Skill selection/summarization is delegated to an external retriever decoupled from the policy gradient, and the library is updated independently of the RL objective (E002, E003).
gap.checked_gap: Real but narrower: neighbours EvolveR, SkillRL and Wang-2025 SAGE already move skills into the training loop (E015, E016); the residual is policy-driven (log-prob) selection and a reward bonus for skill use. Whether decoupling from an external retriever is the binding bottleneck is not tested (no embedding-retriever + same RL control).

matches.reason: Opus confirms son55, which is also the run convention for co-evolving skill libraries under RL (r08a EvolveR → C03). A uniform 5-field JSON schema with a 220-char cap is a canonical conditioning format (step 1). The policy is trained on SKILL:-prefixed prompts to read it (step 3). Steps 4–5 (category holdout, cheap-baseline isolation) are evaluation gaps, not identification failures. sol's generative_process_redesign is rejected: the paper does not liberate a conventionally fixed component of an iterative generative procedure; it retrieves conditioning text, and sol itself found no sub-card fit.

rs_pattern.reason: Skills retrieved by policy log-probability and prepended to the prompt condition inference without per-task updates. That is adapt_via_conditioning/C03 with an RL upstream phase teaching the model to read the schema.

assessment.evidence_level_note: The library evolved during training is retained and read at evaluation (son55:E012). The frozen-seed-library variant (w/o O_{G+1}) scores lower on held-out benchmarks. The hierarchical reward's claimed role is not supported as written (opus:O04), and end-to-end selection learning is not carried by Eq. 6.

G.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. 'External retriever, library updated independently of RL' is a concrete limitation, and neighbours are named (EvolveR, SkillRL, SAGE-Wang). SkillRL is listed as a baseline but absent from Table 1, and the decoupling is not shown to be the binding bottleneck.

M.reason: Opus shared correction (both seats 2). The method has three load-bearing ideas. Two are contradicted by the paper's own equations. (i) The hierarchical reward is said to give skill-augmented correct rollouts a higher advantage than unaided correct ones in the same group (opus:O03). But selection is one skill per query for all G rollouts (opus:O01, opus:O02), and the gate is query-level, so groups are {0,1} or {0,2}. Eq. 5's normalisation is scale-invariant, so the reward cannot act as described (opus:O04). (ii) 'The advantage propagates end-to-end through the selection mechanism' is not carried by Eq. 6, which credits only worker tokens (son55:E004, son55:E005). What remains is a plausible, concretely specified distil-and-retrieve chain (summary rollout from τ+, a uniform schema, log-prob scoring). shared_error_corrections.reason: Both seats missed that the hierarchical reward is inert under the paper's own selection rule. The rule gives one skill per query to all G rollouts (opus:O01, opus:O02), with a query-level gate (Eq. 7). So skill-aided and unaided correct rollouts never share a group, and Eq. 5's group normalisation makes {0,2} and {0,1} groups identical (opus:O04). The authors' central rationale (opus:O03) is therefore refuted by their own equations. Combined with son55's own finding that Eq. 6 does not credit selection, M falls below the 2 anchor.
